subcategory_gloss: food microbiology: enumerating viable bacteria by aerobic plate count
domain_rationale: Correctness is decided by microbiological counting practice: which plates of a tenfold dilution series fall in a validated countable range, how the colonies of countable plates at neighbouring dilutions are pooled against the amount of sample actually plated (volume x dilution), when a result becomes an estimate, a less-than at the detection limit or a greater-than, and how it is reported to two significant figures. The deliverable is the laboratory's CFU/g or CFU/mL result, not software behaviour for its own sake, and no compliance regime or billing rule is involved, so Operations would misplace it; Chemistry and Physics do not own colony enumeration.
evidence: instruction.md: symptoms are microbiological results (0.1 mL spread plates ten times low, too-numerous plates reported as less-than, two good dilutions not pooled)
environment/app/docs/apc-sop.md: a numbered laboratory SOP defining countable, crowded and sparse plates, counted dilutions, plated amount and the four result kinds
planned verifier: whole-report comparison of kind and apc per sample against expectations sealed from solution/model.py, derived from the SOP
